what_its_for: Gabapentin enacarbil is used to treat two conditions: (1) Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) – an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, especially at night, and (2) nerve pain (called postherpetic neuralgia) that happens after a shingles infection. It works by calming overactive nerve signals in your body.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with food. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablet – this can cause too much medicine to enter your body at once. Take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Taking it with food helps it work properly.
dosing: For Restless Legs Syndrome: The usual dose is 600 mg once a day, taken with food at around 5:00 PM. For nerve pain after shingles: The usual starting dose is 600 mg in the morning for 3 days, then increased to 600 mg twice a day (morning and evening). Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well your kidneys work, so always follow the dose your doctor prescribes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for the missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original container. Protect from moisture and heat. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicines down the toilet – ask your pharmacist about the best way to throw away unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine – it can increase dizziness and sleepiness and can be dangerous. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires full alertness until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine may make you feel dizzy or lightheaded.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: new or worsening depression, anxiety, or mood changes; thoughts of self-harm or suicide; unusual behavior or aggression; severe dizziness or drowsiness; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction); difficulty breathing; severe skin rash; or if you feel more clumsy or unsteady than usual. Also tell your doctor if you notice any swelling in your hands or feet.
when_it_works: For Restless Legs Syndrome, some people notice improvement within the first few days to a week. For nerve pain after shingles, it may take a few weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking the medicine even if you do not feel better right away, and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first – stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms.
special_populations: Kidney problems: This medicine is removed from your body by your kidneys. If you have kidney disease or are on dialysis, your doctor will give you a lower or less frequent dose. Always tell your doctor about any kidney problems. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness and drowsiness, which can increase the risk of falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits need to be carefully discussed with your doctor. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years old.
